===== n8n-jobs-guidelines-941 Jobs Category Guidelines: Posting and Applying closed False archived False posts 2
-- 1 2020-03-05 staff  The Jobs category connects people and companies hiring n8n talent with community members looking for opportunities. To keep listings useful and reduce spam, follow these rules when posting a role or applying. Posting a job Hiring posts only. Post here if you are hiring for a role or project. “For hire,” “open to work,” and service-promotion posts are not allowed. Include the essentials. Every hiring post, including posts by community hosts, must include the role title, a brief description of the work and requirements, the company or project, and relevant location or time-zone details. Provide a clear way to apply. Include an email address or application form . If neither is available, explicitly invite applicants to contact you by direct/private message (DM/PM). Keep posts genuine and specific. Spam, generic advertisements, and low-effort AI-generated listings are not allowed. Write for the actual role you are offering. Posts that do not meet these requirements may be rejected or returned for revision. About sending direct messages How to send a direct message (DM)? Click the poster’s username or avatar, then Message . Mention the role, briefly introduce yourself, and include a relevant work sample or link. If Message is unavailable, check your trust level or use the listing’s other contact option. Who can send DMs? Brand new accounts can’t send direct messages yet - to unlock

-- 2 2026-11-05   Hi @Manisman , a reliable way to structure this would be to separate the workflow into three connected stages: lead intake, lead management, and execution monitoring. For lead intake, incoming data from different sources should pass through a common validation process. This includes checking required fields, normalizing email addresses and phone numbers, identifying existing contacts, and using AI to categorize leads against defined qualification criteria. Incomplete or uncertain submissions should be routed for human review. For lead management, every lead should have a consistent record containing its source, qualification status, assigned team member, and follow-up history. This makes CRM updates, team notifications, and follow-up scheduling easier to coordinate. It also helps prevent duplicate records and messages to leads who have already responded. For execution monitoring, error handling should account for API failures, rate limits, and interrupted executions. Each stage should record its outcome so failed operations can be retried without repeating actions that have already succeeded.
